x: "Evergreen"Joe Wilson popped up yet again to win the Club Handicap from Will Belderson with Bob Barnes third. Our thanks are due to the officials judges and helpers who once again on a cold day enabled us to hold another Championship.

Ken Bailey seemed to be doing a steady training spin, while the extra miles suited Bernard Eglinton who shows steady improvement on each outing since his return from abroad. Joe Wilson made a strong effort to beat the handicapper once again, but this was not to be his day.

Consequently we were nowhere in the team Championship, although Bob Barnes walked most creditably, considering the absence of support, to finish 12th in 57:24. Gerry Cameron (24th in 60:06) carried off the third individual handicap and Joe Wilson took first Veterans' prize.

In our last issue I asked if there was a trophy available for presentation for our Annual Inter-School Relay and almost before the ink was dry PERCY WILSON, on behalf of himself and brother Joe, produced a fine shield which the Committee has been very pleased to accept.

Those two distance stalwarts Ray Hall and Pat Duncan did their best to screw each other throughout the race with Pat pulling away up the last hill " out of earshot ". Joe Wilson made a fool of the handicapper winning by over a minute and a half.
Two such men are the Wilson Brothers Joe and Percy, both members of the Walking Section. Sixty-one year old Joe, joined Belgrave in September 1939.
Our team of three (Jack Rutland, Tommy Green and Joe Wilson) tied with Leicester W. C. for third place, but our Midland friends took the awards on a lower time aggregate.
Joe and Percy Wilson brought up the rear in 104:24 and 105:52 respectively. The unofficial team result gave Belgrave the verdict over Vidarians 25 - 30.

In the same race Joe Wilson walked his usual sound race to become No. 164 in 21:04:46. Joe needs no introduction and is often at the roadside judging or helping with the feeding, or, indeed, giving his Club vest an airing.

We are saddened to hear that the Percy half of the stalwart Wilson brothers is seriously ill in Bolingbroke Hospital. Percy and Joe featured in our walking teams for many many years and I know that Joe will do all he can to keep the partnership going by conveying to Percy our best wishes for his recovery.

Eventually our lads finished in a procession with five consecutive placings from 18 to 22 and backed up by George Bentley, Joe Wilson and Joe Coleman, we succeeded in taking the Nijmegan Shield with our eight walkers in the first 48, an excellent performance on which all are to be congratulated.
In the early stages, Jack Bidgood Bert Clayton, Jack Baker, Jack Wakeley and George Oliver, walked in a group with Don Heath and Joe Wilson not far away.

Leading the table of 'Brightons' successfully completed since the last war are John Keown with 16 (consecutive); George Beecham with 15; Joe Wilson, Harry Shields and Bernard Eglington with 12 each; Gordon Doubleday with 11 (2 before the war) and Johnny Morris and Dave King with 10 each.

Congratulations to Joe Wilson on becoming a Grade I Walking Judge. Even before he hung up his walking shoes Joe was putting something back into the sport and the Club, particularly with the youngsters.

See how the youngsters and the womens sections are forming thanks to the efforts of Joe Wilson. Much of the individual success has gone to the Kiwi, Graham 'call me Seats' Seatter who, in the space of three months, has ranked himself amongst Britain's best, including our own Carl.

In the walking sphere the "Belles" have been gaining in strength considerably and it will not be too long before they can match the best teams in the country - a testimony to the training given by Carl Lawton and Joe Wilson.

The judges panel was headed by Syd Spencer, who did the job with his usual quiet efficiency. Also judging were evergreen Harold King, Bill True and Joe Wilson, and in the grade III category, Barbara Dunsford.

Amongst the Judges were Joe Coleman, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Syd Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson. Ray Hall together with Fred and Bill were logging them in, the sheets going in to Jack Goswell and Frank Jarvis, assisted by their wives to get out the results.

Referee for the race was past President Ray Hall, whilst Chief Judge was Syd Spencer, also judging were Joe Coleman, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Bill True and Joe Wilson, recording was Frank Webb and of course masterminding the final result in the back room was Jack Goswell ably assisted by Joan.
